extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs; Department of the Interior; congressional overseers and agency administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Annual narrative reports and performance indicators for U.S. Indian agencies (circa 1880), covering population, agriculture, industry, health, education, police, supplies, buildings, and improvements. Used to evaluate agency condition and needs and to request departmental support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Livestock quality and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Condition and numbers of horses, cattle, sheep, hogs, etc.; improvement in size and strength of horses; cattle fat and well herded and corraled; some cattle milked and milk used in families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report gives counts (e.g., 'about 1,200' horses among all tribes) and notes practices (corraling, careful watching and attendance, milking). Notes efforts by agent to stimulate improvements and Indians' promptness in following advice. Also records epizooties and need to condemn unserviceable animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missionary work and religious instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence and extent of missionary activities: Sunday afternoon singing, Bible readings, attendance by employees and some Indians who understand English; plans to increase instruction as Indians learn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what has been established (e.g., 'singing Sunday afternoon, and Bible readings'), attendance levels, and future plans: 'As soon as they can be understandingly instructed in the Christian way, effort in this respect will be increased.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Education — school establishment and pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction of a school-house (adobes being made, foundation being set) designed for both day scholars and boarders; interest from Indians and expected scholar numbers; use of Kindergarten/object-teaching plan and primers; music as an attractive feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include physical progress ('adobes being made'), expected enrollment ('over 150 scholars are already promised'), pedagogy recommendations ('Kindergarten or object-teaching plan'), teacher quality ('good and efficient teachers') and hoped-for outcomes ('rapid advancement').

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital facilities and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Condition of hospital rooms (former rooms abandoned, supplies removed), building with mud/dirt roof subject to flooding; need for a new shingle roof to prevent flooding and improve patient welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report specific defects and planned remedies (e.g., 'A new roof of shingle will... be commenced soon'). Note availability of physician and shortages of medicines when estimates unsupplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary conditions and public health
rubrics_metrics.description: General sanitary condition satisfactory except for prevalent syphilis and episodic outbreaks (whooping cough); physician success in treatment and enforcement of sanitary rules; statistics of cases treated, births, and deaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document disease prevalence ('syphilis... prevails to a large extent'), treatment outcomes ('doctor has been very successful'), enforcement efforts, and numeric reporting ('1,119 cases have been treated; 13 births and 96 deaths' in one report). Use to evaluate need for medical supplies and hospital accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police organization and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence and discipline of police/scouts; efficiency and obedience when properly officered; readiness to travel to remote parts of the reservation; immediate reporting of violations; role in preventing manufacture and sale of liquor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess organization quality ('one of the best organizations we have at this agency'), leadership ('in fine discipline under my lately appointed chief of scouts'), and functional outcomes (enforcement of agent's orders, prevention of 'liswin' manufacture and whisky introduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplies — quality and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and sufficiency of contracted and purchased supplies (beef, flour, etc.): problems with a June beef contract, replacement contractor with good cattle, temporary difficulties obtaining flour, overall sufficiency thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report contract performance and corrective actions ('beef delivered on the contract of 1879... was poor... new contractor on the 1st of July with cattle of good quality'). Include notes on shortages and resolution ('some difficulty in getting a sufficient amount of flour during June, but it was obtained of good quality').

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident reporting and response to depredations
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation of killings, attacks, raids, thefts, and disturbances; investigation procedures (sending chief of scouts to ascertain truth); recording of arrests, sentences, and claims against government for property losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dates, parties involved, immediate responses (troop movements, scouts), outcomes (deaths, arrests, sentences), and considerations for compensation/claims ('it is probable a claim will be made against the government for this property'). Use to evaluate law-and-order and intergovernmental responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agriculture — reservation farming strategy and yields
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach to cultivation (community farm vs individual allotments), acreage under crops, estimated yields for community and private plots, impact of limited arable land and swamp claims, and obstacles from settlers' livestock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide acreage and crop breakdowns (e.g., '625 acres in wheat, 64 in oats... estimated yield... 7,500 bushels of wheat for the community'), explain rationale for communal farming ('works most of the land by a community of interest'), and note institutional barriers (unpaid settler improvements preventing division of land).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock counts, condition, and transport suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed counts and serviceability ratings for horses, mares, colts, mules, oxen, cattle, hogs; assessment of whether teams are available to haul freight (e.g., insufficient teams to draw one ton).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include serviceability categories (serviceable work, unserviceable work, serviceable saddle) and remark on losses from disease ('severe type of epizooty') and military standards for condemnation. Use counts to evaluate logistic capacity and needs (e.g., harness shortage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation capacity and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of available teams for freight, reliance on commercial transport at prevailing rates, and how transport costs affect agency economics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether agency/Indian-owned teams can meet transport needs ('perhaps... there might be found one team of 4 horses that could draw one ton'), and note dependence on outside carriers and their rates which may make freight uneconomical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements — land clearance and farm/industrial school development
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority and actions to clear land for agency farm and industrial school (e.g., 'two hundred and fifty acres have been cleared, and plowed'); hoped-for benefits as sources of remuneration and in educating Indians to efficient labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record acreage cleared and plowed, link improvements to intended outcomes (remuneration, education), and note that short tenure in charge may limit reporting completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency buildings and structural conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Condition and types of agency buildings (adobes, framed houses, mud roofs, etc.), number of framed/brick houses versus cheap makeshift buildings, need for replacements, and building work performed by Indian carpenters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize repairs, new housing constructed ('Seven houses have been built for the Indians'), deficiencies ('many of our buildings must soon be replaced'), and specific vulnerable features (rotten rails, decayed flumes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grist-mill operations and financial output
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantity of wheat ground for agency, Indians, and others; total weight/bushels processed; cash earnings and tolls in wheat; equipment needs (e.g., 'a new turbine wheel will be required this coming winter').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide production totals (e.g., 'grist-mill has ground 301,970 pounds for the agency... total of 869,229 pounds'), associated earnings and in-kind payments, and maintenance/upkeep needs to sustain operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saw-mill production and operational risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Feet of lumber cut, accidents affecting output (boiler crown sheet collapsed), need to move the mill as nearby timber becomes exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report output ('136,359 feet of lumber'), accidents and their consequences, and strategic concerns such as depletion of local timber and need to relocate the mill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian industry, employment, and vocational training
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which Indians engage in labor (few subsist by the chase), requirement for able-bodied males to work, presence of assistant trades (blacksmiths, carpenters, millers), wages earned for outside work, and industrial education at schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that many Indians command good wages working for others, record available trade positions ('two assistant blacksmiths... two assistant carpenters'), and link industrial training to future expansion of trades as facilities permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: School outcomes — manual-labor and boarding schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance of manual-labor boarding schools: attendance numbers (e.g., average of 18 pupils), marked improvement in labor department (girls sewing and housework), and combined academic and labor instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report months of operation, student proficiency in both studies and labor, plans to expand boarding/manual-labor schools as funds permit, and use of school planting/labor (e.g., 'several acres of potatoes').

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilization measures and social practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators of 'civilization': wearing citizens' dress, possession of furniture and sewing machines, house clothing making ability, marriage relation stability, and challenges in changing loose ideas about marriage and divorce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document social metrics ('All of these Indians wear citizens' dress'), efforts to change marriage customs (legal divorces, 'mutual obligation' marriages), and cultural obstacles to Christianization and civilized habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer conduct and protections for Indian laborers
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidents of fraudulent payment and abuse by employers, trafficking in liquor, necessity of enforcement actions and arrests to check abuses, and trend toward fairer payment in money rather than 'trash'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include case examples (worker paid with wine and then shot), departmental/legal remedies pursued (arrests, prosecutions), and outcomes such as improved employer practices and public sentiment against liquor traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population enumeration and outreach responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Population accounting by families and individuals served, including Indians living off-reservation in various counties; recommendation that these be visited and encouraged to send children to school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use weekly reports and U.S. census to estimate numbers (e.g., '214 heads of families and 534 Indians that drew flour'), list counties where Indians reside, and emphasize outreach frequency and education promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation land usability and resource constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveyed acreage and the portion usable for farming (e.g., '102,118.19 acres included; of that balance, 7,448 acres, all but 2,000 is rough and mountainous; 2,500 lie in this valley and about 1,200 cultivated'); timber resources often inaccessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide acreage breakdowns, explain geographic limitations (mountainous, rocky, swamp claims), note inaccessibility of timber for lumber manufacture due to lack of roads and cost, and implications for economic viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to medical care and hospital accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of attending physician, forward estimates for medicines that went unanswered, difficulty providing proper care without supplies, and requests for limited hospital accommodations for distant sick who must return unable to travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document forwarded estimates ('Carefully prepared estimates for medicines were forwarded... but no reply has been made'), quantify treated cases and need for shelter ('make special request... for limited hospital accommodations'), and link to improved sanitary outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schooling access, funding and consolidation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization and fitting up of school buildings for larger settlements, hope that consolidation of scattered tribes on reservations will allow better educational provision, and limited reach of new schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note departmental authorization status and timelines ('authority has recently been granted... to fit up two buildings... It is hoped that, by October 1, next, these schools will be started'), and argue for consolidation to maximize educational effect.
